title: fallback-fastpath-precision-toggle-safe-mode: fast-path gating, precision toggles, and safe-mode for correctness/perf tradeoffs
author: Lucas Nguyen
description: Summary: Add a guarded fast-path gating system, runtime precision toggles, and a cluster-level safe-mode policy to trade correctness vs performance for the GPU inference runtime. Motivation: The existing fused fast-path kernels (FP16/quantized) provide large throughput and p95 improvements in common workloads but occasionally produce numerical edge-case regressions on long-context attention patterns and certain custom operators. Customers running strict correctness SLAs require deterministic fallbacks while platform SLOs want to retain fast-path benefits for tolerant workloads. This PR introduces three coordinated capabilities: 1) Fast-path gating: a deterministic gate that enables the optimized kernels only when model+input heuristics and runtime checks pass. Gate criteria are: model architecture fingerprint, sequence-length distribution, operator compatibility table, and a lightweight dynamic correctness probe during KV-cache warmup. 2) Precision toggles: API- and config-level toggles to force FP32/FP16/INT8 execution per-deployment, per-model, or per-route. Toggles are implemented as a runtime policy that the kernel selection layer consults. 3) Safe-mode: a cluster-wide policy that enforces conservative defaults for high-SLA customers and allows staged rollouts (canary -> regional -> global). Design notes: The gate is implemented in rust/crates/runtime/src/fastpath.rs as a small decision DAG that must be O(1) per request and cacheable per-model and per-KV-key. We added a periodic re-evaluation window to handle changing sequence distributions. Precision toggles are surfaced via the deployment config proto and exposed through the control plane; the runtime applies them at request dispatch time. When the gate fails, the request falls back to the stable slow-path kernel path with full-precision semantics and identical functional tests. We also integrated a short correctness probe that runs on a small sample of warmup requests to detect numerical drift; if drift is detected beyond threshold, the gate flips to disabled for that model instance and emits an alert metric. Performance impact: Microbenchmarks show 1.6x-1.9x throughput improvement and 15%-30% p95 latency reduction on medium-length sequences when the fast-path is enabled. End-to-end regression test suite shows no correctness regressions when fast-path is gated off. Rollout plan: merge -> canary on dedicated cluster (10% traffic) for 48h -> monitor metrics (token-error-rate, p95 lat, KV cache hit-rate, numerical-drift-alerts) -> increase to 50% -> global rollout. Also included is an emergency rollback knob to disable fast-path at cluster level. Testing: unit tests for gate logic, integration tests verifying kernel selection, end-to-end tests comparing model outputs for 1000 seeded prompts, and a perf harness run with continuous-batching traces. Backwards compatibility: default behavior preserves previous semantics (fast-path allowed) but customers can opt into safe-mode via deployment config or we can apply safe-mode for high-SLA customers by default. Files changed include small interface and decision additions; no breaking API changes to SDKs. See release_notes for operator-facing notes.

feat(precision): implement runtime precision toggle and config proto + control-plane hook

review_comments: Amelia Ross: Please add a short section in the design explaining why the probe uses sampling vs deterministic test cases; how often is the probe run?
Author (Lucas): Probe frequency is configurable; default is per-instance during first 50 warmup requests and then every 10k requests per instance. Added config and docs line.
Priya Kaur: The fallback path adds ~5% CPU on scheduler hot paths; can we move probe work to worker threads?
Author (Lucas): Moved the probe work into the worker-local thread and added a non-blocking offload; updated scheduler.rs accordingly.
Diego Ramos: Can we add a metric for times the gate flipped due to detected drift? Operationally useful.
Author (Lucas): Added fastpath_gate_flips_total and a histogram for drift magnitude. Metrics are emitted to the control plane and appear in the per-model dashboard.
Amelia Ross (LGTM): Tests look good, please squash and merge after CI green.
ci_checks: Perf harness: pass (1.8x median throughput on canary hosts)
release_notes: Added runtime fast-path gating to avoid numerical regressions while preserving fast kernels; introduced precision toggles (FP32/FP16/INT8) and a cluster-level safe-mode policy for conservative production rollouts. Operators can enable/disable fast-path and configure probe frequency. No breaking API changes; rollout via canary is recommended.
